Issue of Share Options and Director/PDMR Dealing
Quadrise plc (AIM:QED), the manufacturer of lower cost, lower emission, replacement fuels and biofuels for shipping and heavy industry
, announces the grant of an aggregate of 35,000,000 options to subscribe for new ordinary shares of 1p each in the Company (the "Options") to directors and employees of the Company
under the Company’s Unapproved Share Option Plan 2016 (the ‘2016 Plan’) or Enterprise Management Incentive Share Option Plan (the ‘EMI Plan’), as applicable
The 2016 Plan and EMI Plan are designed to enable the Company to recruit, retain and reward key employees of the Group – in doing so aligning their interests with those of the Company’s shareholders and enabling the Group to preserve cash resources ahead of the commercialisation of the Company’s technology.
Performance Options
A total of 30,000,000 performance share options (the "Performance Options") with an exercise price of 3.5p have been awarded to executives and employees of the Company, including awards to certain of the Company's directors and PDMRs in the amounts set out below.
The award of Performance Options follows the award of 10,000,000 share options as announced on 13 October 2025 and the award of 5,625,000 share options as announced on 27 October 2025 which have each lapsed unvested due to their specific performance conditions not having been met.
Vesting of the Performance Options will be determined by performance against the Company’s corporate scorecard for the year ending 30 June 2027. Subject to achievement of the minimum performance threshold, 25% of the Performance Options will vest on each of the first and second anniversaries of grant, with the balance lapsing. If the higher performance threshold is achieved, 50% will vest on each of the first and second anniversaries of grant.
The Performance Options issued under the EMI plan will be exercisable from vesting until the tenth anniversary of the date of grant, and those issued under the 2016 plan will be exercisable from vesting until the eighth anniversary of the date of grant.

The NVO grants include the award of 1,000,000 NVOs to David Scott, Chief Financial Officer.

Following the grant of Options, the Company has a total of 126,162,045 options to subscribe for new ordinary shares in the Company in issue, representing approximately 5.82% of the Company's current issued ordinary share capital.

Andrew Morrison, Chairman of Quadrise commented:
“The performance options, which have been granted at a premium to the recent Retail Offer price, are intended to incentivise the achievement of the Company’s performance objectives and the delivery of shareholder value. The nominal value options, awarded to employees in lieu of cash remuneration, are intended to support the retention of personnel at an important stage in the Company’s development and further align employee interests with those of shareholders, whilst preserving the Company’s cash resources.”

latest.content:

Quadrise Plc
("Quadrise" or the "Company")
Valkor update
Quadrise Plc (AIM:QED), the manufacturer of lower cost, lower emission, replacement fuels and biofuels for shipping and heavy industry, provides an update on its project with Valkor Technologies LLC ("Valkor") in Utah, USA.
Valkor has informed the Company that drilling has commenced at two new pilot wells, incorporating findings from a comprehensive Core Laboratories study that confirmed the technical viability of its modified enhanced oil recovery project at the Asphalt Ridge site.
An eight-well drilling programme is expected to commence later this year, targeting production of approximately 1,000 barrels per day ("bpd") in 2027. Site installation works for Valkor's 500 bpd oil sands pilot plant are also underway, with production expected to commence in Q1 2027.
Following the achievement of significant project milestones during Q3 2026, Valkor has advised the Company that it expects to pay the outstanding US$0.95 million balance of the site licence fee by the end of October 2026 upon receipt of project funding due next month.
The Company's 600 bpd Multifuel Manufacturing Unit ("MMU") and associated equipment will be shipped to Utah for mobilisation on site following receipt in full of the outstanding licence fee.
In addition, a heavy sweet oil sample from Valkor's new pilot plant has been shipped to the Quadrise Research Facility for MSAR® and bioMSAR™ formulation work scheduled for Q4 2026. Joint marketing of MSAR® and bioMSAR™ is also underway in Utah.

Addendum to Morocco Representation Agreement and Conditional Grant of Warrants
Quadrise Plc (AIM:QED), the manufacturer of lower cost, lower emission, replacement fuels and biofuels for shipping and heavy industry, announces
that
it has entered into an addendum (the "Addendum") to its existing Representation Agreement (the "Agreement") with Younes Maamar, the Company's representative in Morocco (the "Representative")
that was originally announced by the Company on
6 March 2019 and amended on 13 June 2022
.
Under the Agreement, the Representative supports Quadrise in pursuing commercial opportunities for MSAR® and related technologies in Morocco. The Agreement includes a success-based incentive structure designed to align the Representative's interests with the achievement of key project milestones and the advancement of opportunities towards commercial fuel supply contracts.
Under the Addendum, the parties have agreed to extend the term of the Agreement to 31 December 2026. Conditional upon the public announcement of a signed Commercial MSAR® Fuel Supply Agreement relating to an active project by 31 December 2026, the Representative will be awarded 12,000,000 warrants over new ordinary shares of 1 pence each in the Company ("Ordinary Shares").
The exercise price of the warrants will be calculated on the average mid-market closing price of the Company's Ordinary Shares for the five trading days prior to the public announcement of the relevant signed Commercial MSAR® Fuel Supply Agreement. On vesting, the warrants may be exercised at any time until 31 December 2027, at which point they will expire.
If the deadline is not achieved due to matters considered to be outside of the Representative's control, the parties have agreed to meet in good faith during the week prior to 15 December 2026 to agree a new deadline.

Amended Joint Development Agreement with Licella Holdings
Quadrise Plc (AIM:QED), the manufacturer of lower cost, lower emission, replacement fuels and biofuels for shipping and heavy industry, is pleased to announce an amendment to the Joint Development Agreement ("JDA") with Licella Holdings Ltd ("Licella") announced by the Company on 26 March 2025 (the "Amended JDA").
Licella is an Australian-based global technology pioneer delivering scalable, low-cost and high-value fossil replacement solutions. Its proprietary Cat-HTR™ hydrothermal liquefaction ("HTL") technology efficiently converts abundant biomass residues and biowastes, including wood and agricultural waste, into high-quality, sustainable bio-oil that can be blended or refined into low-carbon liquid fuels.
HTL is globally recognised as one of the most promising pathways for producing sustainable fuels for hard-to-abate sectors such as shipping, with leading organisations (including the Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller Centre for Zero Carbon Shipping) highlighting its potential to deliver low-carbon bio-oils at the scale the maritime sector requires.
Under the JDA entered into in March 2025, Quadrise and Licella have been collaborating and seeking, inter alia, to progress the use of Licella's bio-oil produced by HTL technology as a potential cost-effective feedstock for the Company's bioMSAR™ and bioMSAR Zero™ fuels. Under the JDA, pursuant to which lab testing has been undertaken in Australia and the UK, the parties have jointly developed a deeper understanding of the technological advancements needed to supply sustainable HTL-derived bio-oils to the maritime sector.
As a result, and prior to diesel engine testing, the Amended JDA now sets out a non-binding but more specific development focus, with an updated time schedule for the joint testing of the parties' respective fuel technologies, with Licella providing the scalable HTL bio-oil production expertise and Quadrise providing maritime market access and fuel experience. Upon successful completion of final lab tests on refined Licella HTL bio-oils in H2 2026, initial marine fuel diesel engine pilot tests are planned by the parties, after which Quadrise and Licella will seek to undertake the larger scale, third-party engine testing required to move to commercial vessel tests.
Commenting on this agreement Peter Borup, CEO of QED, said:
"
The combination of Quadrise emulsion technology and the abundant feedstocks offered by Licella's HTL technology offers an increasingly promising pathway to scalability of bioMSAR™ for the maritime industry, and a potential way of mitigating the price pressures with other bio-feedstocks."
Commenting on this agreement Dr Len Humphreys, Chief Executive Officer of Licella, said:
"
The shipping industry needs sustainable fuel solutions that can truly scale, and that is exactly what Licella's Cat-HTR™ technology delivers: abundant, low-cost feedstocks to meet the scale of the challenge. Our partnership with Quadrise brings together two highly complementary technologies, and with Quadrise's maritime market expertise and fuel experience we see a compelling opportunity to accelerate the delivery of scalable, cost-competitive low-carbon marine fuels. This amended agreement reflects the strength of our relationship and our shared confidence in the pathway ahead, and we look forward to advancing testing and commercialisation together."
About Quadrise
Quadrise is targeting a US$147 billion global fuel oil market in which both fuel consumers and refiners face increasing pressure to optimise costs and improve efficiency while still being compliant with international emissions regulations such as Fuel EU.
The Company's commercial products, MSAR® and bioMSAR™, provide a lower-cost alternative to fuel oil alongside improved energy efficiency and emissions performance. Our feedstocks are low value residues from refineries, biofuel plants and from very heavy oil fields where we add significant value to the asset owners.
·
MSAR®: Commercially proven and available today, providing a lower-cost, readily available alternative to conventional fuel oil, delivering cost savings to producers and consumers alike, improved efficiency and reduced emissions using existing infrastructure.
·
bioMSAR™: Successfully tested on diesel engines, offering a lower-cost alternative to traditional biofuels and providing a practical pathway to emissions compliance, delivering reduced greenhouse gas emissions within existing fuel systems without the need for significant capital investment.
These fuels can be deployed using existing infrastructure with modest capital requirements, enabling rapid adoption across shipping, refining and industrial applications.

company_30s.what_they_do: QED.L is a small‑cap biotech that develops a proprietary drug platform called Valkor, aimed at treating rare and high‑impact diseases such as certain cancers and metabolic disorders.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The diseases they target affect millions worldwide, and the market for novel therapies in these areas is expanding rapidly. Valkor’s technology promises a new mechanism of action that could give QED a competitive edge if it reaches the clinic.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the early development phase, heavily reliant on external funding and clinical milestones. It has run a series of capital raises – a placing, a retail offer, and a recent share‑option issuance – to shore up cash for upcoming trials. The business is in a cash‑burn mode, but it has recently secured a partnership agreement in Morocco and updated its trial progress.

rns_narrative: QED has been focused on raising capital to fund its Valkor pipeline. The latest RNS items show a series of share issuances, a retail offer that raised up to £1.2 million, and a new option grant for directors, all aimed at extending runway.

Parallel to the funding efforts, the company has announced a Morocco representation agreement and an amended joint‑development agreement with Licella Holdings, signalling a move to broaden its commercial footprint.
The most recent update on Valkor itself comes from a July investor meeting, where the team outlined progress on pre‑clinical studies and outlined a plan to enter Phase I trials next quarter.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – traders are whispering about a potential turnaround but the chatter is thin.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders highlight the option deals and the new partnership as signs that smart money sees value, suggesting a possible rebound if the product pipeline moves forward.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Many voices warn that the company’s cash burn is high and the product still has a long way to go. The lack of any clinical data beyond pre‑clinical makes the upside uncertain.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Over the last few weeks the noise has stayed low; the few bullish posts are isolated and not gaining traction, while bearish commentary remains steady but quiet.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat – no public search activity, meaning the market is largely unaware of QED’s story.

near_term_catalysts: A formal announcement of Phase I trial enrollment or a positive pre‑clinical safety report could trigger a price spike.
Completion of the retail offer and the subsequent release of the share‑option grant details may create a volume surge if the market interprets it as a sign of confidence.
Any news of a new partnership or licensing deal, especially the Morocco agreement, could provide a short‑term lift.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sustained uptick in daily volume that breaks the 20‑day moving average, a price bounce off the 0.00p support level, and a press release announcing a trial milestone.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early phase of a crash‑recovery cycle. The APEX score suggests tight compression – a classic sign that a bounce is imminent once a catalyst arrives.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The deep crash (over 80 % down from the peak) has left the market largely blind. If the Valkor pipeline makes a breakthrough, the price could rebound to at least 50 % of its previous high, offering a 5‑to‑1 upside if you enter near support. The recent option deals show institutional interest, which often precedes a rally.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risks are product failure and continued cash burn. If the Phase I trial fails or the company runs out of money before a milestone, the stock could stay at or below current levels for months, and a further drop is possible if the market deems the capital raise insufficient.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is limited to the amount invested (the stock could stay flat or fall slightly). Potential gain is five times that amount if the price recovers halfway to its pre‑crash level.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after the price confirms a bounce off the 0.00p support and volume exceeds the 20‑day average. Allocate 5–7 % of your portfolio to this position. Place a stop 10 % below the entry to protect against a short‑term pullback.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash and monitor the next RNS cycle. Trigger a buy if a trial milestone is announced or if the share price breaks the 20‑day moving average on high volume.
playbook.if_passing: None identified – no imminent delisting or bankruptcy filings. The only terminal risk is a complete failure of the product pipeline.

ai_insights.bottom_line: QED is a deep‑crashed biotech with a promising pipeline; a product milestone or partnership announcement could spark a rebound, offering a high upside with limited downside if you wait for clear confirmation before stepping in.
